_about: Embraer EMB-135 (ERJ-135 ER/LR/KE/KL), from Embraer's Airport Planning Manual APM-145/1238, Revision 14 (Nov 29/24): 2.2 Airplane Dimensions (page index 17), Figure 2.2.1 Airplane General Dimensions (page index 18), Figure 2.7.1 Door Clearances (page index 27-28). The figure is drawn at 10.721 pt/m (its 24.39 m fuselage, 26.33 m overall length and 20.04 m span agree within 0.02%): rendered at scale 19.806, to the EMB-145 raster's scale. The EMB-145's placed points (e145/) moved by the two plugs out (plug.py: 2.01 m at 9.0 m, ahead of the wing, from the printed nose-to-main-gear 12.43 m against 14.44 m; 1.53 m at 18.0 m, behind it, the rest of the 3.54 m: the baggage door moves 3.51 m by the door figures) and snapped; laid over each other, the wing moves 2.01 m and the tail 3.54 m as these plugs say. Scaled by the printed 24.39 m fuselage length. A T-tail with two AE 3007 nacelles on stub pylons, plain wing tips. The side view draws 13 cabin windows (one in the overwing exit), the main door and the overwing exit; the baggage door (left side, Figure 2.7.1) at the EMB-145's height less the plugs; the right side's service door from Figure 2.7.1 (its middle 6.17 m from the nose, 0.69 m wide, 1.47 m tall).

sources.title: Embraer, EMB-135 Airport Planning Manual (APM-145/1238, Revision 14, Nov 29/24), 2.2 Airplane Dimensions, Figure 2.2.1 Airplane General Dimensions, Figure 2.7.1 Door Clearances
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off Figure 2.2.1's side, plan and front views (tools/trace/e135/: the EMB-145's points moved by the two plugs and snapped onto this figure); the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. ICAO's E135 also covers the ERJ-140 (its own shape, E135-erj140).
